new_scholarship.name: PTDF Overseas Postgraduate Scholarship Scheme (MSc/PhD)
new_scholarship.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund, a Nigerian federal government agency, sponsors fully funded MSc and PhD places at its partner universities in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia for Nigerian candidates in oil and gas related disciplines. The published benefits for the 2026 award are return flight tickets, health insurance, tuition and bench fees where applicable, and allowances for accommodation and living expenses. Application is made through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal. The 2026 call closed on 27 February 2026 and the Fund has not yet published the 2027 call.
new_scholarship.deadline: Six weeks from the date of publication of the call (2026 call closed 27 February 2026)
new_scholarship.application_period: 2026 cycle: call published 18 January 2026, applications closed 27 February 2026
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Nigerian citizens who hold at least a Second Class Upper (2:1) first degree (or 2:2 with relevant industry experience for MSc), have completed the mandatory National Youth Service Corps, hold five O-Level credits including English Language and Mathematics, are computer literate, and have a verified National Identity Number.
eligibility: Nigerian citizen with a Certificate of Indigeneship / Local Government Identification Letter
MSc: minimum Second Class Upper (2:1) first degree, or Second Class Lower (2:2) with relevant industry experience
PhD: at least Second Class Lower (2:2) first degree plus a good postgraduate degree
Mandatory National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) completed
Five (5) O-Level credits including English Language and Mathematics
Computer literate
Verified National Identity Number (NIN) before application; NIMC verification charges apply
Programme of study consistent with the applicant's prior academic background and relevant to the oil and gas industry
coverage: Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
benefits: Tuition and bench fees where applicable
Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
requirements: Only PTDF-approved courses at PTDF partner institutions are eligible

UK PhD awards for the 2026 academic year are limited to split-site programmes at the College of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Kaduna (CPESK) with Robert Gordon University, University of Strathclyde or University of Portsmouth
PhD applicants intending to apply under the PTDF/DAAD partnership in Germany must secure a research supervisor before final selection interviews
Lecturers applying must submit a letter from their Vice-Chancellor confirming they are not benefiting from any other scholarship
MSc: Statement of Purpose of maximum 500 words
PhD: research proposal of maximum five pages covering topic, background, objectives, methodology and data collection approach
required_documents: First Degree Certificate or Statement of Result
WAEC/GCE/SSCE/NECO results and relevant PINs for online verification
Evidence of membership of relevant professional associations
application_method: Create an applicant account on the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng
Complete and submit the online application form with all documents scanned in PDF format
Shortlisted applicants are invited to a selection interview and must present transcripts in advance
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Initial screening is based on submitted qualifications, after which the top applicants in each category from each State are invited to interview. A selection committee assesses academic merit (quality of degrees, complete academic transcripts, relevant professional qualifications), relevant publications for PhD applicants, membership of professional bodies, and the viability and relevance of the study plan or research proposal. Multiple applications result in automatic disqualification, as does submission of illegible or falsified documents.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Nigerian graduates with a strong oil and gas academic record who have completed NYSC and are seeking a funded MSc or PhD at a PTDF partner university in the UK, Germany, France or Malaysia.

new_scholarship.name: GETFund Postgraduate Local Scholarship (2026/27)
new_scholarship.description: The Ghana Education Trust Fund, a statutory Ghanaian education fund, has announced that applications for its 2026/27 Postgraduate Local Scholarship will open on Monday 5 October 2026 and close on Friday 27 November 2026. The scheme covers candidates pursuing Master's and PhD programmes within Ghana and is separate from the Fund's foreign scholarship programme. The Fund states that financial support to Scholars includes tuition fees, accommodation and scholastic materials. Applications are made only through the GETFund Scholarship Portal at scholarships.getfund.gov.gh.
new_scholarship.application_period: Monday 5 October 2026 to Friday 27 November 2026 for the 2026/27 academic year
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be pursuing a Master's or PhD programme in the 2026/27 academic year and apply through the official GETFund Scholarship Portal, which carries the detailed eligibility criteria, documentation requirements and application process. The Fund describes its postgraduate support as covering candidates described as 'brilliant but needy'.
eligibility: Pursuing a Master's programme in the 2026/27 academic year
Pursuing a PhD programme in the 2026/27 academic year
Applying through the official GETFund Scholarship Portal at scholarships.getfund.gov.gh
Uploading scanned copies of all required supporting documents for vetting and shortlisting
benefits: Social and academic support to Scholars alongside the financial support
application_method: Visit the official GETFund Scholarship Portal at scholarships.getfund.gov.gh
Create an account and complete the online application form with accurate information
Upload scanned copies of the relevant supporting documents
Submit through the portal before the closing date; submissions sent through any other channel will not be processed
new_scholarship.selection_notes: GETFund states that the selection process is rigorous and transparent, with shortlisted applicants contacted after vetting and shortlisting is completed. The Fund also warns that all official correspondence is directly between the Fund and the applicant.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Ghanaian postgraduate candidates in the 2026/27 academic year who need tuition, accommodation and study materials to complete a Master's or PhD within Ghana.
new_scholarship.notes: Announced in a single notice together with the GETFund Undergraduate Local Scholarship, which runs on the same 5 October to 27 November 2026 timeline. A separate GETFund Postgraduate Foreign Scholarship for 2026/27 was announced on 14 April 2026 with a window of 13 to 30 April 2026 and is not open.

rejected.candidate: PNG Tertiary Education Study Assistance Scheme (TESAS), Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology
rejected.reason: Fully verified and genuinely open on the awarding body's own pages: TESAS 'provides financial assistance on behalf of the Government of PNG to eligible students of targeted tertiary education programs on a merit basis as verified through the National Online Selections System', covers 'tuition fees, board and lodgings, travel, and student resources', runs AES, HECAS, Gender Equity and postgraduate awards, and the 2027 national selection cycle opened 11 August 2026. Withheld from this file only because Papua New Guinea is in Oceania and the brief's region enum (Europe / United States / Canada / Australia / New Zealand / Asia / Latin America / Africa / Middle East) has no Oceania value; labelling it Australia or Asia would be a false fact, and it is outside this cell's African and Asian bias. The scheme is a strong candidate for any Oceania-labelled shard and no DHERST or GoPNG body appears in this shard's dedup list.
Same awarding body as the two published GETFund records but a closed cycle: applications ran 13 to 30 April 2026 and the Fund publishes no later window, so it is not an open or upcoming award

rejected.candidate: Zambia HELB Scholarship opportunities (Higher Education Loans and Scholarships Board)
rejected.reason: The Board's own opportunities page lists only one scholarship, the Moroccan Vocational Scholarship Program, marked 'Closed' with a 27 May 2025 deadline; the open windows on the board's homepage are student loans, which are excluded

rejected.candidate: Tanzania Samia Scholarship 2026/2027 (Ministry of Education, Science and Technology)
rejected.reason: The ministry's official call exists and is dated 28 July 2026, but the announcement body carries no text and the entire call sits in an attached PDF that returned raw uncompressed PDF bytes through both webfetch and the browser PDF viewer, so the deadline, award value and eligibility could not be read from the awarding body and would have had to be invented

rejected.candidate: Bolashak Scholarship Program for Studying at Universities in Kazakhstan (JSC Center for International Programs)
rejected.reason: The operator's own page confirms the programme, quota (490 Bachelor's, 50 Master's, 10 PhD places) and an application window of 30 March to 31 May 2026 via studyin.kz, but it publishes no statement of what the award pays for, so tuition and living coverage cannot be set without inventing facts

The official pages give the programme's purpose and its 2005 government decree establishing the operator but publish neither the current intake window nor the benefit schedule; the only dated intake figure I could find came from a university advertisement, which is not an official awarding-body source

rejected.candidate: Fiji Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service (TSLS), Ministry of Education
rejected.reason: The statutory body is confirmed on its own site as established under the Tertiary Scholarship and Loans Act 2014 and funded by the Government of Fiji, but its application portal currently states 'Sorry, there are no programs', so there is no open cycle to record

rejected.candidate: PNG National Online Application System (NOAS) 2027 selection cycle, DHERST
rejected.reason: Confirmed open (cycle opened 11 August 2026) but it is an admission selection portal into registered in-country higher education institutions with no funding attached, so it is not a funding award

rejected.candidate: HEC national and international scholarship programmes (Higher Education Commission of Pakistan)
rejected.reason: The Commission lists 43 schemes including the Coastal Region Higher Education Scholarship Program for Balochistan, the Undergraduate Scholarship Program for Gilgit-Baltistan and the Prime Minister's Fee Reimbursement Scheme, but the listing page exposes no per-scheme URLs, no published window and no benefit wording, and the application portal at scholarship.hec.gov.pk is behind a CNIC login, so nothing could be confirmed to record standard

rejected.candidate: Uganda Ministry of Education and Sports scholarship calls
rejected.reason: Every current call on the ministry's own scholarship page is a foreign government's award (Algeria, Serbia, Pakistan, Cyprus, Egypt, Al-Azhar and the UK Commonwealth), so the ministry is the intermediary rather than the awarding body, and the schemes are already covered elsewhere in the catalogue

rejected.candidate: Indonesia LPDP scholarship (Lembaga Pengelola Dana Pendidikan, Ministry of Finance)
rejected.reason: Three attempts across webfetch and two browser sessions all returned ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT from this network, so no field could be confirmed from the awarding body

rejected.candidate: Thailand Government Scholarship and Philippine DOST S&T graduate scholarships
rejected.reason: thaigovscholarship.com returned ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED and dost.gov.ph's S&T scholarships page would not complete loading after repeated attempts; aggregator-only descriptions were not used

rejected.candidate: Mauritius Africa Scholarships Scheme (Ministry of Education and Human Resources, Tertiary Education Commission)
rejected.reason: The ministry page still publishes only the 2017, 2018 and 2019 editions of the scheme, with no current cycle

rejected.candidate: Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) Foreign Postgraduate Scholarship 2026/2027
rejected.reason: The Commission's own domain timed out on every attempt through both webfetch and the browser, and the widely reported 19 April 2026 deadline came only from aggregators
The university's homepage carries a generic scholarships link but no distinct funding award with a published window was confirmed within the fetch budget
